heading: The guide states the instrumentation model backwards and never names the plugin
title: Rewrite the Bun guide's instrumentation step around @sentry/bun/plugin
body_html:
The Bun guide at guides/bun/index.mdx:94 and :106 tells the user to run bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js, and the alert at :96-100 states that Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code and that bundling requires manual instrumentation. @sentry/bun/plugin is not named anywhere on the page, and logs is used as an onboarding block at :182 but is missing from the options at :20-22.

What was observed on bun 1.4.0: a bundle built with Bun.build({ plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] }) from @sentry/bun/plugin records library and framework spans, while running the same app unbundled with bun run records none. packages/bun/src/plugin.ts:14 states the plugin is build-only. The unbundled diagnostic message is printed only with debug: true.

What to change:

  • Keep the --preload step, described as what guarantees init order.
  • Add a "Build with the Sentry plugin" step showing Bun.build({ entrypoints: [...], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] }) imported from @sentry/bun/plugin.
  • Replace the alert at :96-100 with a plain statement: library and framework instrumentation requires a build with the plugin; bun run on unbundled source records manual spans plus Bun.serve, node:http and fetch spans.
  • Add logs to the onboarding options at :20-22, or remove the block at :182.

Source: runtime docs audit, item DOC-B1

heading: Stream-mode includes call `'static'` the default; develop defaults to `'stream'`
title: Fix inverted traceLifecycle default in the stream mode includes
body_html:
The three stream-mode includes present stream mode as opt-in. platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.bun.mdx:5 (and javascript.deno.mdx:5, javascript.cloudflare.mdx:8) say "Opt in by setting the traceLifecycle option to 'stream'", and each closes with "set traceLifecycle to 'static' (the default)" (javascript.bun.mdx:25, javascript.deno.mdx:24, javascript.cloudflare.mdx:62).

On develop the default is 'stream'. packages/core/src/client.ts:242 normalizes traceLifecycle: options.traceLifecycle === 'static' ? 'static' : 'stream', so every value except an explicit 'static' resolves to stream. No runtime overrides this, and packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-serve.ts:28 describes 'stream' as the default too.

What to change

  • Reframe all three includes as opt-out: 'stream' is the default, 'static' is what a user sets.
  • Replace the traceLifecycle: "stream" sample lines with "static" examples, or drop them.
  • Add the missing comma after tracesSampleRate: 0.2 at javascript.cloudflare.mdx:19.

heading: Deno crons page recommends denoCronIntegration(), which throws on Deno 2.9
title: Stop recommending denoCronIntegration() on the Deno crons page
body_html:
platform-includes/crons/setup/javascript.deno.mdx:1 heads its first section "Automatic Check-Ins (Recommended)" and :12 tells the reader to pass Sentry.denoCronIntegration() to Sentry.init.

That call crashes startup on current Deno. packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-cron.ts:23 assigns Deno.cron = new Proxy(Deno.cron, ...), but on Deno 2.9.0 Deno.cron is a getter-only property, so Sentry.init throws TypeError: Cannot set property cron of #<Object> which has only a getter. This reproduced in four separate audit runs. Line 18 returns silently when Deno.cron is missing, so without --unstable-cron the integration is a no-op. It is also not in the default set at packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:31-49, contrary to its JSDoc at deno-cron.ts:64.

What to change

  • Remove the "Recommended" framing and the denoCronIntegration() snippet, or label the integration as broken on Deno 2.9.
  • Lead with the Sentry.withMonitor / Sentry.captureCheckIn sections already on the page.
  • State that Deno.cron needs --unstable-cron.

heading: Bun OpenTelemetry setup includes import @sentry/node-core and call APIs that no longer exist
title: Rewrite the Bun OpenTelemetry setup includes against develop
body_html:
Three Bun OpenTelemetry includes are written against a package and APIs that no longer exist. platform-includes/performance/opentelemetry-setup/javascript.bun.mdx:5 and :48 import SentryContextManager, validateOpenTelemetrySetup from @sentry/node-core; error-monitoring-only/javascript.bun.mdx:3 and with-custom-sampler/javascript.bun.mdx:3 do the same. javascript.bun.mdx:12 and :55 pass skipOpenTelemetrySetup: true, and error-monitoring-only/javascript.bun.mdx:30 calls provider.addSpanProcessor(...).

On develop there is no node-core package under packages/. skipOpenTelemetrySetup, SentryContextManager, validateOpenTelemetrySetup and SentrySpanProcessor appear nowhere in packages/*/src. @sentry/opentelemetry exports only getScopesFromContext, SentryPropagator, SentryTracerProvider, setOpenTelemetryContextAsyncContextStrategy and registerPrepareSpanScope (packages/opentelemetry/src/index.ts:1-9). The Bun option is enableOpenTelemetrySetup (packages/bun/src/types.ts:23), and addSpanProcessor was removed in OpenTelemetry JS 2.x.

What to change

  • Drop every @sentry/node-core import and the removed symbols.
  • Replace skipOpenTelemetrySetup: true with enableOpenTelemetrySetup: false.
  • Replace provider.addSpanProcessor(...) with the constructor's spanProcessors array.

heading: Agents SDK page claims instance-name span attributes and instance-name conversation IDs; neither is true
title: Correct the Agents SDK span attribute and conversation ID claims
body_html:
docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/agents-sdk.mdx:10 says callable RPC spans carry "the agent class and instance name as attributes". :39 says "The automatic conversation ID defaults to the agent instance name", and :41 builds override guidance on that premise, warning about per-user instances and singletons named "default".

Neither claim holds on develop. packages/cloudflare/src/instrumentations/agents/types.ts:61-70 builds the span attributes from instance._ParentClass?.name alone, setting gen_ai.agent.name to the base agent class; no instance name is attached. The conversation id is a uuid4() minted per instance and persisted to Durable Object storage (types.ts:173, :180), rotated to a fresh uuid4() when message:clear fires (instrumentChatAgentConversation.ts:34-36). types.ts:104 says the instance name is deliberately not used.

What to change

  • Fix :10 to name only the agent class attribute.
  • Rewrite the Conversation IDs section around a generated uuid4 per instance that rotates on chat clear.
  • Replace the "default" / per-user override rationale, which rests on the false premise.

Source: runtime docs audit, item DOC-R13

heading: The Cloudflare Vite plugin reads its options from an undocumented file and is a silent no-op without the wrangler config path
title: Document the instrument.server file and the wranglerConfigPath requirement on the Cloudflare Vite plugin page
body_html:
guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx and the proposed quick start step 3 present sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() as a drop-in: add it next to cloudflare(), build, deploy. Neither says where the SDK options come from when the plugin wraps the entry, and neither says what happens when the wrangler config is not named wrangler.jsonc or wrangler.toml at the project root.

Observed on develop with a Worker whose source has no withSentry call: the plugin wraps the entry at build time (const viteEntry = withSentry(__SENTRY_OPTIONS_CALLBACK__, __SENTRY_DEFAULT_EXPORT__) in the built output), and the options callback is taken from an instrument.server.{ts,js,mjs,cjs} file next to the wrangler main. Without that file the callback falls back to () => undefined and the Worker runs with no DSN, silently. With the wrangler config under a non-default name and no wranglerConfigPath, the plugin instruments nothing: the run produced an empty sink, an uncaught error in the worker log and no trace headers, with no warning from the plugin. With wranglerConfigPath set and the options file present, the built Worker delivered the same errors, spans, headers and logs as a hand-written withSentry, with no experimental flag.

What to change:

  • On the Vite plugin page, add the instrument.server.ts file as a required step when the source has no withSentry, with its shape: a default export of the options callback.
  • State that wranglerConfigPath is required whenever the config is not at the default path, and that the plugin does nothing without it.
  • Remove the _experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection flag from the page and from guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:77-92; it is not needed on develop (also DOC-C4).

Source: runtime docs audit, item DOC-Q2, quick start QS-cloudflare, variant vite

heading: Remix on Cloudflare: documented wrong
title: Rewrite the Remix on Cloudflare page for Workers and fix the Vite plugin options
body_html:
docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/remix.mdx is 60 lines and does not describe a working Workers setup: :39-49 installs only @sentry/remix with no @sentry/cloudflare, and :55-58 embeds the shared include. In that include, the Cloudflare branch at platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.remix.mdx:263-313 covers Cloudflare Pages only, and the "Capture Server-Side Errors" step at :315-347 sits outside any PlatformSection and tells every reader to import from bare @sentry/remix at :333. Separately, guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:30-47 presents _experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection as required.

Verified on the develop line: Remix v2 (2.17.5) with the Remix Vite plugin on workerd, compatibility_date: "2026-05-01", compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]. Install @sentry/remix and @sentry/cloudflare. In app/entry.server.tsx, export const handleError = sentryHandleError imported from @sentry/remix/cloudflare. In the worker entry, Sentry.withSentry() from @sentry/cloudflare around a handler built with createRequestHandler(instrumentBuild(remixBuild)). In vite.config.ts, sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() from @sentry/cloudflare/vite at its defaults alongside the Remix plugin, with ssr: { target: 'webworker', noExternal: true }.

Works today:

  • Loader, action and resource-route errors, parameterized route names with http.route, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans with propagation headers, db spans from mysql, Sentry.logger logs.

Known limits:

  • Importing from bare @sentry/remix in a webworker SSR build leaves handleError undefined and captures nothing.
  • A route with no loader or action stays method-only.
  • Without sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() there are no database spans and no warning; mysql2 is unusable on workerd.

What to change:

  • Rewrite guides/cloudflare/frameworks/remix.mdx: add @sentry/cloudflare to the install at :39-49, add a Workers entry section, point handleError at @sentry/remix/cloudflare, and add a database-spans section.
  • Correct guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:30-47 to the shipped buildTimeInstrumentation and autoInstrumentation options, both defaulting to true.

heading: Elysia on Cloudflare: documented wrong
title: Add an Elysia on Cloudflare Workers page and drop the Bun/Node-only runtime claim
body_html:
No page mentions Elysia on Cloudflare Workers. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25 lists the prerequisites as "Bun or Node.js 18+ (with @elysiajs/node adapter)" and the install snippets at :55-56 and :82 are Bun and Node only. platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12 has a "Runtime Behavior" section covering exactly two runtimes. The Cloudflare framework list at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 has no Elysia entry and guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ has no elysia.mdx.

Verified on the develop line: Elysia 1.4.30 on workerd with compatibility_date: "2026-05-01" and compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]. Install @sentry/cloudflare @sentry/elysia elysia. Construct the app as withElysia(new Elysia({ aot: false })) before any route is registered, and export Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), { fetch: request => app.fetch(request) }). Ahead-of-time compilation must be off: with the default, workerd refuses to start the Worker because Elysia's generated handler runs new Function and touches randomness in global scope. For database spans, build with Vite: plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()] from @sentry/cloudflare/vite, then vite build and point wrangler at the emitted config.

Works today:

  • Unhandled errors via Elysia's global error hook, parameterized route names, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans with headers, Sentry.logger logs, and db spans through the Vite build.

Known limits:

  • A wrangler-bundled Worker emits no database spans.
  • withElysia must wrap the instance before routes are registered, or only the error path gets the route name.
  • mysql2 on workerd needs disableEval: true in the connection options.

What to change:

  • Add docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/elysia.mdx with the wiring above and list it at guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23.
  • Add a Cloudflare Workers entry to guides/elysia/index.mdx:25 and to the Runtime Behavior list at platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12.

heading: Elysia on Deno: documented wrong
title: Document Elysia on Deno: init from @sentry/deno, keep withElysia
body_html:
docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25 lists prerequisites as Bun or Node 18+ with the node adapter, and the install and configure snippets at :52-70 and :78-120 have only Bun and Node tabs, with Sentry.init imported from @sentry/elysia. platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12 enumerates exactly two runtimes and :6 claims parameterized route names unconditionally. A grep for deno over the Elysia guide returns nothing.

Verified on Elysia 1.4.30 and Deno 2.9.0: install the packages with npm into a real node_modules, set {"nodeModulesDir": "manual"} in deno.json, then call Sentry.init() from @sentry/deno before Deno.serve and import only withElysia (and fetchIntegration) from @sentry/elysia. Mount with Deno.serve({ port }, withElysia(new Elysia()).get(...).fetch). Add import "@sentry/deno/import"; as the first line for database spans, and pass integrations: [fetchIntegration()] for outgoing requests.

Works today:

  • Route errors, mechanism auto.http.elysia.on_error.
  • GET /users/:id with op http.server and source route.
  • Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
  • Outgoing http.client spans plus sentry-trace/baggage, with fetchIntegration().
  • Database spans for mysql, and logs.

Known limits:

  • @sentry/elysia's own init() delegates to @sentry/bun and does not instrument Deno.serve: with it there is no http.server span, every request shares one process-wide trace, and incoming trace headers are ignored.

heading: Nuxt on Deno: documented wrong
title: Correct the Nuxt Nitro preset page for Deno: keep the node-server preset
body_html:
docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:7 claims that the SDK supports different Nitro deployment presets, "most of which work out of the box", and the 11-line file then documents only Cloudflare Pages at :9-11. The Nuxt guide has no Deno mention anywhere, so a reader picking the deno_server preset gets no warning.

Verified on Nuxt 4 with @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 and Deno 2.9.0: do not set a Nitro preset. Build the default node-server output with npx nuxt build, keep sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import' } in nuxt.config.ts and a root sentry.server.config.ts that calls Sentry.init(), then run the output under Deno with cd .output/server && PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./index.mjs. Nitro's node-server entry uses node:http, which the SDK instruments on Deno. For outgoing requests, add winterCGFetchIntegration() from @sentry/vercel-edge to Sentry.init.

Works today:

  • Errors from nitro route handlers, with request data and source context.
  • Parameterized GET /api/users/:id with source route.
  • Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
  • http.client spans and sentry-trace/baggage on fetch and nitro's $fetch, with the integration above.
  • Logs.

Known limits:

  • With nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' } there is no request instrumentation at all: no http.server spans, getActiveSpan() is undefined in handlers, every request shares one isolation scope and one trace id so tags and users leak, and incoming trace headers are ignored.
  • Outgoing fetch is not instrumented on Deno without the integration above.

What to change:

  • guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:7: qualify the "work out of the box" claim; add a Deno section next to Cloudflare Pages at :9 with the run command and the deno_server warning.
  • Cross-link a Deno framework page for Nuxt.

heading: Astro on Bun: documented wrong
title: Name Bun in the Astro runtime alert and add a Running on Bun section
body_html:
The runtime alert at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:21-28 says the SDK "currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions" and that other non-Node runtimes are not supported, which reads as excluding Bun. Nothing under guides/astro/ mentions Bun, and nothing under guides/bun/ mentions Astro.

Verified on Astro 7.3.1 with the @astrojs/node standalone adapter and @sentry/astro 10.67.0 on Bun 1.4.0: the sentry() integration in astro.config.mjs, a root sentry.server.config.mjs guarded with Sentry.isInitialized(), astro build, then bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs. The preload is required, because the integration injects the init only into .astro page chunks. Install @sentry/bun and add its fetchIntegration() to the server init, guarded on typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined' so Node deployments of the same build do not double-count.

Works today:

  • Unhandled page and endpoint errors via the Astro request middleware
  • Route names GET /users/[id] with source route and http.route
  • Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
  • Incoming sentry-trace/baggage continuation
  • Outgoing fetch spans and propagation headers, with fetchIntegration() added
  • Sentry.logger log envelopes

Known limits:

  • Database spans are not recorded on Bun in this setup.

What to change:

  • guides/astro/index.mdx:21-28: amend the alert to name Bun as working on the Node adapter output.
  • Add a "Running on Bun" section to that page with the bun --preload ... dist/server/entry.mjs start command, the runtime-gated fetchIntegration(), and the capability list.

heading: Astro on Deno: documented wrong
title: Correct the Astro runtime note: Deno with @deno/astro-adapter works
body_html:
docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:22-31 carries an Alert titled "What runtime do you use?" saying the SDK only works on Node runtimes such as the Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions, pointing Cloudflare users elsewhere, and calling other non-Node runtimes not supported. That reads as excluding Deno. grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/ returns zero hits, and guides/deno/ never mentions Astro.

Verified on Astro 7.3.1 in SSR mode (output: 'server') with @deno/astro-adapter 0.6.0 and @sentry/astro 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: install the packages with npm install into a real node_modules rather than deno add, set deno.json to {"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}, add the sentry() integration in astro.config.mjs, keep a root sentry.server.config.js that calls Sentry.init(), add a src/middleware.ts whose first line imports that config, build normally and run the built dist/server/entry.mjs with Deno.

Works today:

  • Route errors, mechanism auto.middleware.astro, with request URL and source context.
  • GET /users/[id] with source route, in both trace lifecycles.
  • Per-request isolation across concurrent requests.
  • Incoming sentry-trace/baggage continuation.
  • Database spans for mysql2, injected by the Vite plugin @sentry/astro adds during astro build.
  • Logs.

Known limits:

  • Outgoing fetch() is not instrumented on Deno: no http.client span and no sentry-trace/baggage headers, so the downstream service starts a new trace. Adding fetchIntegration from @sentry/cloudflare in sentry.server.config.js, or using node:http/node:https, restores both.

What to change:

  • guides/astro/index.mdx:22-31: amend the Alert to name Deno as a supported runtime and link out.
  • Add a Deno framework page for Astro with the @deno/astro-adapter setup, the middleware import and the fetchIntegration snippet.

heading: SvelteKit on Deno: documented wrong
title: Correct the SvelteKit adapter note: adapter-node runs on Deno
body_html:
docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/manual-setup__v10.7.0.mdx:21-35 holds the "Notes on SvelteKit adapter compatibility" section, whose "Currently not supported" bullet at :30-31 says non-Node server runtimes are not yet supported, while :28 lists adapter-node as fully supported. That reads as excluding Deno, and the current manual-setup.mdx has no adapter-and-runtime section at all. grep -rni deno over the SvelteKit guide returns nothing.

Verified on SvelteKit with adapter-node and @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: build with vite build under Node, using sentrySvelteKit() imported from @sentry/sveltekit/vite, then start the adapter output with HOST=<host> PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi build/index.js. For outgoing requests, register fetchIntegration from @sentry/cloudflare, already installed as a dependency of @sentry/sveltekit, in src/hooks.server.js, gated on Deno so Node builds are not double-instrumented.

Works today:

  • Errors from +server.js handlers, mechanism auto.function.sveltekit.handle_error.
  • GET /users/[id] with source route.
  • Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
  • http.client spans plus sentry-trace/baggage, with fetchIntegration().
  • Database spans for the mysql driver, with no extra flags.
  • Logs.

Known limits:

  • Without fetchIntegration(), neither a global fetch() nor SvelteKit's event.fetch produces an http.client span or carries trace headers on Deno.
  • mysql2 cannot be loaded once the SDK is initialized: Deno compiles require('*.json') as JavaScript while a module hook is registered (denoland/deno#36240), and the route fails with SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'.

What to change:

  • Fix manual-setup__v10.7.0.mdx:21-35 to name Deno with adapter-node as supported.
  • Restore an adapter-and-runtime section in manual-setup.mdx and add a Deno framework page with the run command and the fetchIntegration snippet.
